jobs.title: Managing Director, Business Development, National Corporate Partnerships
jobs.description:
Managing Director, Business Development, National Corporate Partnerships (Full-time)

POSITION REPORTS TO
: Jerry Ochoa, Vice President, National Corporate Partnerships

PRIORITY APPLICATION DEADLINE
: Friday, August 14th. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis after this deadline.

LOCATION
: Flexible

What You'll Do

We are looking for a Managing Director, Business Development to lead Teach For America's pursuit of new national corporate partnerships and to build the next generation of corporate partnerships that fund Teach For America's mission. In this role, you will set the vision, strategy, and pipeline that fuel our corporate business development engine, and you will personally lead the cultivation and closing of six- and seven-figure new corporate partnerships that advance TFA's mission.

The ideal candidate will be energized by the blank-page work of business development. You find where TFA's mission intersects a company's priorities, design partnership models that don't yet exist, and build the case that moves a prospect from cold to closed. You are at ease with senior corporate leaders, from C-suite executives to heads of CSR and corporate foundations, and you translate those relationships into meaningful, mission-aligned investments. You bring a sharp strategic mind, deep fluency in the corporate philanthropy landscape, and a proven track record of closing new business at scale. You will be equally comfortable in the boardroom and in the weeds of a prospect pipeline. You bring curiosity and openness to how emerging technologies — particularly AI — can accelerate your work, and you approach these tools with fluency, critical thinking, and a strong ethical grounding.

The goal is to secure new, high-value corporate partnerships that expand TFA's national revenue base and deepen our long-term financial sustainability. For the current fiscal year, the team charge will be between $3M-$5M in new money.

What You'll Be Responsible For

Business Development Strategy and Vision (20%)

Set the annual and multi-year strategy for new corporate revenue, including national goals, target sectors, and priority prospect lists.
Build and maintain the business development team's infrastructure, KPIs, and workflow management processes.
Develop annual priorities and tactics that grow TFA's corporate revenue base and align to organizational fundraising goals.

Prospect Pipeline Management and New Business Acquisition (40%)

Lead the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and closing of new national corporate partners, with a focus on six- and seven-figure opportunities.
Serve as primary strategist and central relationship manager for prospective corporate partners across the pipeline.
Serve as the primary external representative of TFA to prospective corporate funders, including C-suite leaders, corporate foundation executives, and heads of CSR/ESG functions.
Manage a personal portfolio of high-priority prospects, ensuring rigorous move management from qualification through close.
Oversee the transition of newly closed partners to the Account Management sub-team to ensure a best-in-class donor experience.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Enterprise Development (15%)

Forge and foster deep partnerships with regional fundraising teams and national colleagues to build mutually beneficial pursuit strategies that reflect national and regional priorities.
Leverage TFA's network of national and regional board members, senior leaders, and program teams to open doors and advance prospects.
Contribute to enterprise-wide development mindsets and donor-centered strategies across TFA.
Lead complex, cross-functional project management to move prospects through the pipeline and deliver on partnership commitments.
Explore, develop, and responsibly apply AI tools to strengthen prospect research, pipeline management, proposal development, and internal workflows — modeling curious, ethical, and critically-minded use of emerging technology for the sub-team and the broader NCPT.

People Management and Team Culture (15%)

Manage and develop your direct report (for our current fiscal year this will likely mean managing one Director on the Business Development sub-team) toward their annual new-revenue goals.
Onboard, coach, and empower direct reports to grow as professional fundraisers and to meet their pipeline and revenue targets.
Build an equitable and inclusive sub-team culture within Business Development that reflects TFA's core values.
Support the professional growth and long-term trajectory of direct reports.

Contribution to Team, Development, and Organizational Culture (10%)

Contribute to a collective culture of excellence, teamwork, Core Values leadership, and commitment to DEI on the NCPT, National Development Team, and across the organization.
Participate in special projects (e.g., economic model sprints, cross-team initiatives such as the Lead Now Fund).
Step into leadership and facilitation opportunities at the Development team and organization level.
Speak with respect and courage when necessary to improve processes, culture, and mindsets aligned to TFA's Foundations and Core Values.

A WEEK IN THE LIFE

Over the course of any week, the Managing Director, Business Development will spend time:

Preparing for and leading cultivation and solicitation meetings with corporate prospects and their senior executives.
Coaching direct reports on pipeline strategy, prospect management, and prospect communications.
Building and refining pitch decks, partnership proposals, and other high-stakes donor-facing materials.
Experimenting with and applying AI tools to accelerate research, drafting, analysis, and preparation — and sharing learnings with the team.
Partnering with the VP, NCPT and MD, Account Management to align on team goals, pipeline health, and cross-portfolio strategy.
Collaborating with regional fundraising leaders on shared prospects and cross-cutting opportunities.
Tracking pipeline progress and revenue projections in Salesforce and other reporting tools.
Representing TFA at external convenings, industry events, and executive briefings.

Your Experience

Your areas of knowledge and expertise that matter most for this role (minimum qualifications):

Ability to build and manage a high-performing corporate business development function, from strategy through execution.
Expertise in the corporate philanthropy, corporate social responsibility, and/or corporate partnerships landscape.
Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to identify, prioritize, and pursue high-value opportunities.
Proficient in senior-level relationship management, including engaging with C-suite executives and corporate foundation leaders.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including proposal writing, executive briefings, and pitch delivery.
Rigorous project and pipeline management skills, with the ability to move complex opportunities through long sales cycles.
Strong people management skills and ability to develop direct reports.
Deep commitment to TFA's mission, values, and commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusiveness.
Education: Bachelor's degree required.
Proficient in Microsoft Office; experience with Salesforce required.
Curiosity and openness to emerging technologies — including AI tools — with the fluency, critical thinking, and ethical grounding to explore, evaluate, and responsibly apply them in daily work.

BONUS (preferred Qualifications)

Prior Experience

At least 7 years of fundraising experience, business development, or strategic partnerships experience with a strong track record of closing six- and seven-figure gifts or deals.
Prior management experience, including managing to ambitious revenue goals.
Experience in the education sector or in mission-driven nonprofit fundraising.
Experience navigating complex, national organizations with matrixed local and central teams.
CFRE (Certified Fund-Raising Executive) certification, MBA, or other advanced degree preferred.

Work Demands

Travel up to 3–4x per quarter for internal and external meetings.
Occasional evening and weekend work required to support high-stakes cultivation and solicitation activities.

Skills

Best-in-class client service orientation and follow-through.
Ability to be entrepreneurial and flexible in a fast-paced, results-oriented culture.
Strong ability to influence others toward outcomes without direct authority.
Positive, can-do approach and ability to bring hopefulness and optimism to the team.
Prior experience integrating AI tools into fundraising, sales, communications, research, or knowledge management workflows.

YOUR FUTURE TEAM

The National Corporate Partnerships Team (NCPT) is one of five sub-teams on TFA's National Development Team. Our charge is to strengthen, grow, and create new corporate partnerships that maximize financial and broader contributions to TFA's mission and long-term sustainability. The Business Development sub-team leads the pursuit of new national corporate partners, working in close partnership with the Account Management sub-team, regional fundraisers, and enterprise-wide leaders. Under a five-person structure of VP + 2 MDs + 2 Directors, this MD will lead the BD function and directly shape TFA's growth in a rapidly evolving corporate philanthropy landscape. NCPT is an AI-forward sub-team, actively exploring how emerging technology can deepen partner relationships, sharpen strategy, and expand our capacity — and we're looking for leaders who share that curiosity.

Your Compensation

The applicable salary range for each U.S.-based role is based on where the employee works and is aligned to one of 3 tiers according to a cost-of-labor index in that geographic area. Starting pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. New hires are typically brought into the organization at a salary between the minimum and the salary range, depending on qualifications, internal equity, and the budgeted amount for the role. The expected salary ranges for this role are set forth below. These ranges may be modified in the future.

Tier A: $90,000 - $118,100

Tier B: $98,000 - $128,700

Tier C: $106,100 - $139,300

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role

As Chief Operating Officer at Parachute Health, you own the company's operating system. We are at a growth inflection, moving from a single core product to a multi-product platform, and executing landmark payor and channel partnerships that multiply our delivery load. The company's strategy, products, and pipeline are strong; the constraint on our next chapter is operational: converting commitments into flawless delivery, running the execution cadence that keeps a scaling organization coherent, and making service quality a competitive weapon rather than a liability.

This is an internal-facing, execution-first executive seat, engineered to complement a specialized leadership team. You do not own field selling (CRO), growth architecture or strategic partnerships (CGO), the revenue-operations and commercial-systems stack (EVP Revenue Operations, reporting to the CFO), or finance (CFO). You own everything that turns their work into delivered, retained customer value: implementations and delivery, customer support and service, program management, platform operations, and the company-wide operating cadence. You are the integrator — the leader who orchestrates across functions so the CEO can stay focused on product, market, and the external agenda.

Responsibilities

Company Operating System

Operating cadence: Design and run the company's execution rhythm — operating reviews, cross-functional planning, and the accountability system that keeps every function on plan.
Company scorecard: Drive execution against the company scorecard and KPIs — consuming the commercial source of truth the EVP Revenue Operations maintains, and ensuring every team knows its number and its path.
Cross-functional orchestration: Break ties, clear blockers, and sequence initiatives across departments; own the seams between functions where execution goes to die.
Annual operating plan: Translate strategy into the annual operating plan and quarterly commitments, in partnership with the CEO, CFO, and functional leaders.
Automation-first operations: Partner with our Chief AI officer to embed AI and automation throughout the operating functions — absorbing rising volume with flat or sublinear headcount, and treating automation as the default answer before adding heads.

Delivery, Implementations & Client Operations

Implementation engine: Own end-to-end customer implementations across suppliers, health systems, and payors — including the surge capacity our 2026 payor go-lives demand — with predictable timelines and quality.
Delivery economics: Own the economics of delivery — on-time and on-budget performance, implementation cost, and the direct line from go-live velocity to revenue recognition. Implementation speed is revenue at our transaction-based model; you treat it that way.
Service transformation: Own customer support and service quality end-to-end, with a mandate to materially improve clinician retention, strengthen enterprise escalation management, and build the service operation into a retention weapon. This is the seat's defining first-year deliverable.
Proactive service model: Move service from reactive to proactive — instrumented client-health scoring, early-warning signals, and playbooks that catch at-risk accounts before they churn, built with the lifecycle instrumentation the EVP Revenue Operations maintains.
Client operations: Run the operational functions that serve live customers day-to-day, with clean handoffs to the account-management and customer-success organizations that own the relationships.
Program management: Own company-level program management for the initiatives that cross functional lines.

Organizational Scale & People (Interim)

Scaling infrastructure: Build the operational infrastructure — processes, systems, capacity planning — for an organization doubling revenue and headcount.
People bridge: Hold the People function on an interim basis until the Chief People Officer is seated (CPO will report to the CEO), ensuring no drop in hiring velocity or team health during the transition.
Operational talent & culture: Build, coach, and retain the operations leadership bench — several senior operating leaders will report into this seat — and own the culture and retention of the frontline operations workforce, where attrition quietly destroys service quality.

Executive Partnership

CEO integrator: Serve as the CEO's primary operating partner — absorbing the internal orchestration load so the CEO focuses on product, market-reading, and the external agenda.
With the CRO: Deliver the implementation and service quality that protects the number she wins; own the operational side of retention.
With the CGO: Operationalize landmark partnerships post-signature — the delivery infrastructure that makes channel pull-through real.
With the CFO & EVP Rev-Ops: Run execution on the instrumentation they build; feed operational reality back into forecasting and planning.

The profile we're hiring

Execution discipline: Trains run on time under you. You have built operating cadences, delivery engines, and service organizations that perform predictably at scale — and you are personally allergic to slipped commitments.
Strategic foresight: You see two or three moves ahead and name constraints before they bite — capacity walls, service debt, integration bottlenecks — rather than reporting them after impact.
Lived scale experience: You have operated through the passage we are in, whether inside a SaaS, network, or healthcare-technology business, and you know which systems break at which milestones because you were there.
Service & delivery depth: You have owned customer delivery, support, or client operations directly — ideally including a turnaround — and can point to the numbers: churn reduced, NPS moved, on-time delivery raised, while volume grew.
Automation-first scaler: You have scaled support and delivery volume with flat or sublinear headcount by deploying automation and AI in production — not as pilots, but as the operating model.
Integrator temperament: High-EQ orchestrator who makes specialized executives better without absorbing their scope; comfortable owning outcomes through leaders you do not control.
Builder's bias: You build systems before you add heads, and you leave every function more scalable than you found it.

Benefits

Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage: Comprehensive plans with options for low-to-no-cost premiums.
Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account.
401(k) Retirement Plan
Equity Incentive Plan
Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance.
Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces.
Flexible Vacation Policy
Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO).
Home Office and Wellness Stipend
Monthly Internet Stipend
Annual Learning and Development Stipend

Job Title:
Citizenship Program Director

Location:
Based in Santa Fe, NM (hybrid eligible; occasional travel to northern & southeastern New Mexico required)

Position Type:
Full-Time (32-hour work week)

Compensation:
Competitive salary commensurate with experience and qualifications and includes a comprehensive benefits package

Reports To:
Executive Director

Organizational Overview

Somos Un Pueblo Unido (Somos) is a 30-year-old statewide community-based racial and economic justice organization dedicated to organizing immigrant families and low-wage workers in seven counties in New Mexico. Our work focuses on building long-term community power, protecting rights, improving economic conditions, and strengthening communities. We employ a range of strategies, including community education, leadership development, litigation, grassroots policy and legislative advocacy, community-based research, voter and civic engagement.

Position Summary

Somos seeks a licensed, bilingual attorney to lead our community-based pro-se citizenship program. The Citizenship Program Director
will manage the program, supervise legal assistants, coordinate a pro se citizenship program in Santa Fe, rural northern, and southeastern New Mexico, provide legal representation in some naturalization cases, and collaborate with Somos staff to expand access to citizenship services. This is a position based in Santa Fe with regular travel to rural communities.

There is flexibility for some remote work.

Key Responsibilities

Legal Services and Program Leadership

Manage a pro se naturalization program that provides group application support and legal guidance to lawful permanent residents applying for U.S. citizenship in underserved rural areas and Santa Fe, including legal screenings, eligibility assessments, and naturalization preparation.
Supervise citizenship legal assistants and volunteers.
Ensure compliance with professional standards and up-to-date practices in immigration and naturalization law.
Maintain accurate records and case management systems to support program evaluation and grant reporting.
Occasionally provide direct legal representation to LPR’s applying for U.S. citizenship.

Community Engagement and Outreach

Coordinate and lead citizenship workshops and naturalization clinics in collaboration with community partners.
Recruit community partners.
Work closely with Somos’ organizing team to integrate citizenship services into broader immigrant rights and civic engagement campaigns.
Deliver community education presentations and trainings related to naturalization, fee waivers, disability exceptions, and language access.

Administration and Advocacy

Contribute to grant proposals and reports for citizenship-related funding.
Track service metrics and outcomes to improve program effectiveness and impact.
Represent Somos in local, statewide, and national advocacy spaces focused on immigrant inclusion and naturalization access.
Support Somos campaigns and policy advocacy.

Qualifications

J.D. and licensed to practice law preferably in New Mexico.
At least 2–3 years of experience in immigration law.
Experience working with pro se applicants or in community-based legal settings preferred.
Experience supervising legal support staff.
Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (required).
Demonstrated commitment to immigrant justice, grassroots organizing, and racial equity.
Willingness to travel to rural northern & southeastern New Mexico and work occasional evenings or weekends. Mileage compensation and car rental options available for work-related travel.

Salary and Benefits

Competitive salary, negotiable based experience and qualifications.
32-hour workweek with full-time benefits
Generous benefits package including:
100% of medical insurance coverage (dental and vision included).
Paid vacation and sick leave.
Paid parental leave.
18+ paid holidays and days off.
401K retirement match plan.

Bar dues and professional development support

by August 15, 2025

Nuestra Organización:

Somos Un Pueblo Unido (Somos) es una organización comunitaria estatal con 30 años de trayectoria dedicada a la justicia racial y económica. Organizamos a familias inmigrantes y trabajadores con bajos salarios en siete condados de Nuevo México. Nuestro trabajo se enfoca en construir poder comunitario a largo plazo, proteger derechos, mejorar las condiciones económicas y fortalecer nuestras comunidades. Empleamos múltiples estrategias, incluyendo educación comunitaria, desarrollo de liderazgo, litigio, incidencia legislativa y política de base, investigación comunitaria, y participación cívica y electoral.

Resumen Del Puesto:

Somos busca a una persona abogada licenciada y bilingüe para dirigir nuestro programa comunitario de ciudadanía pro-se. Director/a del Programa de Ciudadanía será responsable de coordinar el programa en Santa y en comunidades rurales, supervisar a asistentes legales, brindar representación legal en algunos casos de naturalización, y colaborar con el personal de Somos para ampliar el acceso a los servicios de ciudadanía. Este puesto está basado en Santa Fe con algunos viajes a comunidades rurales. Se ofrece flexibilidad para trabajar parcialmente de manera remota.

Responsabilidades Principales:

Servicios legales y liderazgo del programa:

Coordinar un programa de naturalización pro-se que brinda apoyo grupal para completar solicitudes y orientación legal a residentes permanentes legales (LPR) que desean obtener la ciudadanía en zonasrurales desatendidas y en Santa Fe. Esto incluye evaluaciones legales, verificación de elegibilidad y preparación para la entrevista de naturalización.
Supervisar a los asistentes legales y voluntarios del programa de ciudadanía.
Asegurar el cumplimiento de normas profesionales y prácticas actualizadas en leyes de inmigración y naturalización.
Mantener registros precisos y sistemas de manejo de casos para la evaluación del programa e informes para subvenciones.
Ocasionalmente brindar representación legal directa a personas solicitando la ciudadanía.

Participación Comunitaria y Divulgación:

Coordinar y facilitar talleres y clínicas de ciudadanía en colaboración con aliados comunitarios.
Reclutar nuevos aliados y organizaciones comunitarias.
Trabajar estrechamente con el equipo de organización comunitaria de Somos para integrar los servicios de ciudadanía en campañas más amplias de derechos de los inmigrantes y participación cívica.
Ofrecer presentaciones y capacitaciones sobre el proceso de naturalización, exenciones de pago, excepciones por discapacidad y acceso lingüístico.

Administración y Abogacía:

Contribuir a la redacción de propuestas e informes relacionadas con ciudadanía.
Monitorear datos y resultados de los servicios para mejorar la eficacia e impacto del programa.
Representar a Somos en espacios de incidencia a nivel local, estatal y nacional relacionados con la inclusión de inmigrantes y el acceso a la ciudadanía.
Apoyar las campañas y el trabajo de incidencia política de Somos.

Licenciatura en Derecho (J.D.) y licencia vigente para ejercer como abogada/o, preferiblemente en Nuevo México.

Description

Development Director* and Team Lead - School of Engineering

Department: Lawrence Development

Reports to: Assistant Vice President for Development

FLSA Status: Exempt

The final pay will be determined based on several factors, including qualifications, experience, education, and years within the job or industry, with a strong emphasis on maintaining internal equity.

Note: This position will be filled at the Development Director or Sr. Development Director level, commensurate with the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Development Director – At least five years of professional experience in higher education/healthcare fundraising. This may be substituted for seven or more years or professional experience in an area with strong similarities to development work. Major gift experience required. Must have success managing a diverse portfolio.

Sr. Development Director - At least ten years of professional experience in higher education/healthcare fundraising. This may be substituted for ten or more years of professional experience in an area with strong similarities to development work. Major gift experience required. Must have success managing a diverse portfolio.

Who We Are And What We’re About

KU Endowment is an independent, nonprofit organization and the official fundraising foundation for the University of Kansas. We partner with donors in providing philanthropic support to build a greater KU.

As an employee of KU Endowment, you’ll witness firsthand the power of our donors’ generosity. You will join a talented and fun group of people who are inspired to help KU through the support of loyal alumni and friends. This support fuels excellence, enabling students and faculty to develop innovative programs and research that distinguish the university. We connect the philanthropic passions of donors with the needs of students, faculty and programs – and everyone benefits.

People are engaged. Purpose is ignited. Lives are changed.

What We Are Looking For

Full-time professional fundraising position responsible for the organization, implementation, and direction of a comprehensive development program for raising private gifts to The Kansas University Endowment Association in support of the School of Engineering and the University of Kansas. Provides assistance to appropriate University personnel and KU Endowment staff in the coordination, planning, and implementation of fundraising activities of the School of Engineering.

The individual in this position is expected to embrace KU Endowment’s stated core values – passion for KU, partnership with donors, perpetual support for KU, and a people-centered approach – and demonstrate support for them through professional interactions and activities.

Hybrid Work Environment

Following the initial training period, this position offers a hybrid work schedule, with the flexibility to work remotely for part of the week. However, the role requires multiple days per week on-site at our Lawrence, KS office to ensure effective collaboration, team engagement, and alignment with organizational goals.

What’s a typical day look like?

Directs programs for identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of prospective and current major gift donors to the School of Engineering and the University of Kansas working with the dean, department chairs, KU Endowment officers and professional staff, University administrators, faculty, and volunteer leaders.

Crafts and deploys a strategic operational plan – develops and implements both annual and long-range goals, objectives, and strategies to maximize private support for the School of Engineering, consistent with the overall plan of KU Endowment. As a team lead, candidates will demonstrate strong, seasoned, professional experience.
Coordinates preparation and development of major gift proposals to School of Engineering prospects for presentation by the University Chancellor, the Dean of the School, KU Endowment staff, and volunteer leaders.
Supervises the shared development assistant who provides administrative support for this constituent area.
Manages, monitors and mentors two other professional fundraisers supporting the School of Engineering that are focused on strategic identification of prospects and timely and consistent movement through management stages (qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship).
Position requires an extensive amount of time out of the office traveling to meet development goals, as well as attendance at events occurring outside of traditional business hours.
Collaborate with Development Team Leads to identify and implement best practices, align strategies, and support clear communication across the broader Development team.
Regular and reliable attendance is essential for this position.
Performs such other duties as may be assigned from time to time by the Vice President for Development and other senior development staff.

Requirements

What’s required to be considered:

Bachelor’s degree required.
A minimum of five years of successful professional experience in major gift fundraising is required. Higher education fundraising experience is preferred.
Prior management experience is also preferred, particularly experience coaching, mentoring, or supporting the professional growth of individual team members in a fundraising environment.
Excellent written, oral, and communication skills and the ability to work independently, as well as part of a team, are essential.
Must possess the ability to independently initiate, organize and follow through with fundraising strategies.
Must be able to work with minimal supervision and exercise excellent judgement.
Adept at using social media, text, phone, and video conferencing.
Strong work ethic with a desire to continue to learn.
Entrepreneurial spirit and fearless approach to portfolio building and relationship development.
Willingness to step outside one’s comfort zone and embrace challenges.
Excellent organizational skills.
Exceptional interpersonal skills and readiness to engage donors and alumni.
Skilled at navigating and using databases, familiarity with CRM systems, and entering contact reports.
Ability to establish and maintain professional and effective working relationships inside and outside KU Endowment.
Ability to adapt to new procedures and technology.

Self-Motivated: You’re a go-getter who takes initiative and drives projects forward with enthusiasm and determination.
Collaborative: You shine in a team setting. Whether with your colleagues, prospective donors, or campus partners, you’re always finding ways to combine efforts and maximize outcomes.

Creates individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies

Uses fundraising systems and metrics to prioritize work and evaluate portfolio health

Evaluates fundraising effectiveness and benefactor engagement outcomes

Serves as a trusted liaison with benefactors ensuring values‑aligned engagement

Contributes to a collaborative fundraising culture by sharing insights, supporting team strategy discussions, and aligning efforts across campus and central partners
Represents the University professionally in benefactor meetings, campus engagements, and select events, exercising sound judgment and discretion
Exercises sound judgment in managing donor conversations, including independently resolving issues when appropriate and engaging leadership or partners thoughtfully when needed

Overview

Yale New Haven Hospital is seeking an accomplished academic podiatric foot and ankle surgeon to serve as the Program Director of its CPME-accredited Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program. This is a unique opportunity to join one of the nation's premier academic health systems and help shape the education and development of future podiatric surgeons.

As Program Director, you'll provide strategic and educational leadership for a well-established residency program while maintaining an active clinical practice. The role is ideal for a physician who is passionate about resident education, mentorship, academic medicine, and advancing innovation in podiatric surgery. You'll collaborate closely with multidisciplinary faculty across Yale New Haven Health and the Yale School of Medicine, contributing to excellence in patient care, research, and physician training.

Yale New Haven Health is committed to fostering a culture guided by its core values of Integrity, Patient-Centered Care, Respect, Accountability, and Compassion, with a strong emphasis on academic excellence, collaboration, and delivering exceptional care to the communities it serves.

This position offers the opportunity to make a lasting impact on one of the country's respected podiatric residency programs while building an academic career within a nationally recognized healthcare system.

Responsibilities

Educational Leadership

Provide strategic leadership for all aspects of the residency program.
Develop, implement, and continuously enhance a comprehensive competency-based curriculum in podiatric medicine and foot and ankle surgery.
Foster resident development in clinical judgment, surgical technique, professionalism, communication, and lifelong learning.
Promote scholarly activity, quality improvement, and evidence-based practice.
Create a culture of educational excellence, innovation, patient safety, professionalism, and accountability.

Program Administration

Direct the overall administration of the residency program.
Maintain compliance with all Council on Podiatric Medical Education (CPME) accreditation standards, Yale New Haven Health policies, and Yale School of Medicine Graduate Medical Education requirements.
Oversee resident recruitment, orientation, evaluations, promotion, remediation, graduation, and disciplinary processes.
Supervise the Residency Program Coordinator and ensure efficient day-to-day operation of the residency program.
Lead annual program evaluation and continuous quality improvement initiatives.

Ensure comprehensive operative and clinical experience across the full spectrum of podiatric medicine and foot and ankle surgery, including reconstructive surgery, trauma, diabetic limb preservation, sports medicine, wound care, and complex foot and ankle pathology.
Collaborate with faculty to maximize educational opportunities and progressive surgical responsibility.
Promote interdisciplinary education and collaborative patient care throughout the Yale New Haven Health System.

Foster faculty participation in teaching, mentorship, curriculum development, resident evaluation, scholarly activity, and educational innovation.
Support faculty development through mentorship and continuing educational opportunities.

Academic Appointment And Faculty Responsibilities

Provide outstanding clinical and surgical teaching in the operating room, ambulatory clinics, inpatient services, and formal didactic conferences.
Mentor residents in surgical technique, clinical decision-making, professionalism, ethics, leadership, and career development.
Promote scholarly activity through clinical research, quality improvement initiatives, publications, presentations, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Advance the academic mission and national reputation of the Yale New Haven Hospital Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program.

Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM).

Board Certification by the American Board of Foot and Ankle Surgery (ABFAS).

Eligible for appointment to the Yale New Haven Hospital Medical Staff with unrestricted clinical privileges.

Progressive leadership experience in graduate medical education.
Previous experience as a Program Director or Associate Program Director of a CPME-accredited Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program strongly preferred.
Demonstrated success in residency education, accreditation, faculty mentorship, and program development.
Academic appointment or eligibility for faculty appointment within the Yale School of Medicine preferred.

Leadership Competencies

Visionary and collaborative leadership.

Excellence in clinical practice, surgical education, and patient-centered care.
Integrity, professionalism, accountability, and sound judgment.
Strategic thinking, innovation, and continuous quality improvement.

You bring curiosity and openness to how emerging technologies — particularly AI — can accelerate your work, and you approach these tools with fluency, critical thinking, and a strong ethical grounding.

The goal is to secure new, high-value corporate partnerships that expand TFA's national revenue base and deepen our long-term financial sustainability. For the current fiscal year, the team charge will be between $3M-$5M in new money.

Business Development Strategy and Vision (20%)

Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role

As Chief Operating Officer at Parachute Health, you own the company's operating system. We are at a growth inflection, moving from a single core product to a multi-product platform, and executing landmark payor and channel partnerships that multiply our delivery load. The company's strategy, products, and pipeline are strong; the constraint on our next chapter is operational: converting commitments into flawless delivery, running the execution cadence that keeps a scaling organization coherent, and making service quality a competitive weapon rather than a liability.

This is an internal-facing, execution-first executive seat, engineered to complement a specialized leadership team. You do not own field selling (CRO), growth architecture or strategic partnerships (CGO), the revenue-operations and commercial-systems stack (EVP Revenue Operations, reporting to the CFO), or finance (CFO). You own everything that turns their work into delivered, retained customer value: implementations and delivery, customer support and service, program management, platform operations, and the company-wide operating cadence. You are the integrator — the leader who orchestrates across functions so the CEO can stay focused on product, market, and the external agenda.

Responsibilities

Company Operating System

Operating cadence: Design and run the company's execution rhythm — operating reviews, cross-functional planning, and the accountability system that keeps every function on plan.
Company scorecard: Drive execution against the company scorecard and KPIs — consuming the commercial source of truth the EVP Revenue Operations maintains, and ensuring every team knows its number and its path.
Cross-functional orchestration: Break ties, clear blockers, and sequence initiatives across departments; own the seams between functions where execution goes to die.
Annual operating plan: Translate strategy into the annual operating plan and quarterly commitments, in partnership with the CEO, CFO, and functional leaders.
Automation-first operations: Partner with our Chief AI officer to embed AI and automation throughout the operating functions — absorbing rising volume with flat or sublinear headcount, and treating automation as the default answer before adding heads.

Delivery, Implementations & Client Operations

Implementation engine: Own end-to-end customer implementations across suppliers, health systems, and payors — including the surge capacity our 2026 payor go-lives demand — with predictable timelines and quality.
Delivery economics: Own the economics of delivery — on-time and on-budget performance, implementation cost, and the direct line from go-live velocity to revenue recognition. Implementation speed is revenue at our transaction-based model; you treat it that way.
Service transformation: Own customer support and service quality end-to-end, with a mandate to materially improve clinician retention, strengthen enterprise escalation management, and build the service operation into a retention weapon. This is the seat's defining first-year deliverable.
Proactive service model: Move service from reactive to proactive — instrumented client-health scoring, early-warning signals, and playbooks that catch at-risk accounts before they churn, built with the lifecycle instrumentation the EVP Revenue Operations maintains.
Client operations: Run the operational functions that serve live customers day-to-day, with clean handoffs to the account-management and customer-success organizations that own the relationships.
Program management: Own company-level program management for the initiatives that cross functional lines.

Organizational Scale & People (Interim)

Scaling infrastructure: Build the operational infrastructure — processes, systems, capacity planning — for an organization doubling revenue and headcount.
People bridge: Hold the People function on an interim basis until the Chief People Officer is seated (CPO will report to the CEO), ensuring no drop in hiring velocity or team health during the transition.
Operational talent & culture: Build, coach, and retain the operations leadership bench — several senior operating leaders will report into this seat — and own the culture and retention of the frontline operations workforce, where attrition quietly destroys service quality.

Executive Partnership

CEO integrator: Serve as the CEO's primary operating partner — absorbing the internal orchestration load so the CEO focuses on product, market-reading, and the external agenda.
With the CRO: Deliver the implementation and service quality that protects the number she wins; own the operational side of retention.
With the CGO: Operationalize landmark partnerships post-signature — the delivery infrastructure that makes channel pull-through real.
With the CFO & EVP Rev-Ops: Run execution on the instrumentation they build; feed operational reality back into forecasting and planning.

The profile we're hiring

Execution discipline: Trains run on time under you. You have built operating cadences, delivery engines, and service organizations that perform predictably at scale — and you are personally allergic to slipped commitments.
Strategic foresight: You see two or three moves ahead and name constraints before they bite — capacity walls, service debt, integration bottlenecks — rather than reporting them after impact.
Lived scale experience: You have operated through the passage we are in, whether inside a SaaS, network, or healthcare-technology business, and you know which systems break at which milestones because you were there.
Service & delivery depth: You have owned customer delivery, support, or client operations directly — ideally including a turnaround — and can point to the numbers: churn reduced, NPS moved, on-time delivery raised, while volume grew.
Automation-first scaler: You have scaled support and delivery volume with flat or sublinear headcount by deploying automation and AI in production — not as pilots, but as the operating model.
Integrator temperament: High-EQ orchestrator who makes specialized executives better without absorbing their scope; comfortable owning outcomes through leaders you do not control.
Builder's bias: You build systems before you add heads, and you leave every function more scalable than you found it.

Employer HSA Contribution: Company-funded contributions to your Health Savings Account.
401(k) Retirement Plan
Equity Incentive Plan
Annual Company-Wide Bonus: Opportunity for up to 15% bonus based on company performance.
Remote-First Culture: We are remote-first with a dedicated NYC office and reimbursement options for co-working spaces.
Flexible Vacation Policy
Summer Fridays: 5 additional Fridays off during the summer (separate from PTO).
Home Office and Wellness Stipend
Monthly Internet Stipend

Description

Development Director* and Team Lead - School of Engineering

Department: Lawrence Development

Reports to: Assistant Vice President for Development

FLSA Status: Exempt

The anticipated salary for this position starts at $124,100+ for the Development Director role and ranges up to $136,500+ for the Senior Development Director role. The final pay will be determined based on several factors, including qualifications, experience, education, and years within the job or industry, with a strong emphasis on maintaining internal equity.

Note: This position will be filled at the Development Director or Sr. Development Director level, commensurate with the successful candidate’s experience and qualifications.

Development Director – At least five years of professional experience in higher education/healthcare fundraising. This may be substituted for seven or more years or professional experience in an area with strong similarities to development work. Major gift experience required. Must have success managing a diverse portfolio.

Sr. Development Director - At least ten years of professional experience in higher education/healthcare fundraising. This may be substituted for ten or more years of professional experience in an area with strong similarities to development work. Major gift experience required. Must have success managing a diverse portfolio.

Who We Are And What We’re About

KU Endowment is an independent, nonprofit organization and the official fundraising foundation for the University of Kansas. We partner with donors in providing philanthropic support to build a greater KU.

As an employee of KU Endowment, you’ll witness firsthand the power of our donors’ generosity. You will join a talented and fun group of people who are inspired to help KU through the support of loyal alumni and friends. This support fuels excellence, enabling students and faculty to develop innovative programs and research that distinguish the university. We connect the philanthropic passions of donors with the needs of students, faculty and programs – and everyone benefits.

People are engaged. Purpose is ignited. Lives are changed.

What We Are Looking For

Full-time professional fundraising position responsible for the organization, implementation, and direction of a comprehensive development program for raising private gifts to The Kansas University Endowment Association in support of the School of Engineering and the University of Kansas. Provides assistance to appropriate University personnel and KU Endowment staff in the coordination, planning, and implementation of fundraising activities of the School of Engineering.

The individual in this position is expected to embrace KU Endowment’s stated core values – passion for KU, partnership with donors, perpetual support for KU, and a people-centered approach – and demonstrate support for them through professional interactions and activities.

Hybrid Work Environment

Following the initial training period, this position offers a hybrid work schedule, with the flexibility to work remotely for part of the week. However, the role requires multiple days per week on-site at our Lawrence, KS office to ensure effective collaboration, team engagement, and alignment with organizational goals.

What’s a typical day look like?

Directs programs for identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of prospective and current major gift donors to the School of Engineering and the University of Kansas working with the dean, department chairs, KU Endowment officers and professional staff, University administrators, faculty, and volunteer leaders.
Solicits major gifts ($50,000+), both outright and deferred, in support of the stated needs of the School of Engineering.
Crafts and deploys a strategic operational plan – develops and implements both annual and long-range goals, objectives, and strategies to maximize private support for the School of Engineering, consistent with the overall plan of KU Endowment. As a team lead, candidates will demonstrate strong, seasoned, professional experience.
Coordinates preparation and development of major gift proposals to School of Engineering prospects for presentation by the University Chancellor, the Dean of the School, KU Endowment staff, and volunteer leaders.
Supervises the shared development assistant who provides administrative support for this constituent area.
Manages, monitors and mentors two other professional fundraisers supporting the School of Engineering that are focused on strategic identification of prospects and timely and consistent movement through management stages (qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship).
Position requires an extensive amount of time out of the office traveling to meet development goals, as well as attendance at events occurring outside of traditional business hours.
Collaborate with Development Team Leads to identify and implement best practices, align strategies, and support clear communication across the broader Development team.
Regular and reliable attendance is essential for this position.
Performs such other duties as may be assigned from time to time by the Vice President for Development and other senior development staff.

Requirements

What’s required to be considered:

Bachelor’s degree required.
A minimum of five years of successful professional experience in major gift fundraising is required. Higher education fundraising experience is preferred.
Prior management experience is also preferred, particularly experience coaching, mentoring, or supporting the professional growth of individual team members in a fundraising environment.
Excellent written, oral, and communication skills and the ability to work independently, as well as part of a team, are essential.
Must possess the ability to independently initiate, organize and follow through with fundraising strategies.
Must be able to work with minimal supervision and exercise excellent judgement.
Adept at using social media, text, phone, and video conferencing.
Strong work ethic with a desire to continue to learn.
Entrepreneurial spirit and fearless approach to portfolio building and relationship development.
Willingness to step outside one’s comfort zone and embrace challenges.
Excellent organizational skills.
Exceptional interpersonal skills and readiness to engage donors and alumni.
Skilled at navigating and using databases, familiarity with CRM systems, and entering contact reports.
Ability to establish and maintain professional and effective working relationships inside and outside KU Endowment.
Ability to adapt to new procedures and technology.

What separates the best from the rest?

Self-Motivated: You’re a go-getter who takes initiative and drives projects forward with enthusiasm and determination.
Collaborative: You shine in a team setting. Whether with your colleagues, prospective donors, or campus partners, you’re always finding ways to combine efforts and maximize outcomes.
Master Communicator: You have a knack for articulating compelling stories and connecting with donors on a deep level.
Resilient: You stay positive and persistent, turning challenges into opportunities and never losing sight of the mission.
Unwavering Integrity: You build trust through honesty, transparency, and the highest ethical standards.
Growth Mindset: You embrace challenges, see setbacks as learning opportunities and consistently strive to grow in personal and professional endeavors.

Physical Requirements

A valid driver’s license.
Must have access to reliable transportation to travel between multiple locations for training, donor meetings, networking, events and/or work-related activities.
Must be able to respond quickly and effectively to directions and safety hazards.
This job operates in a professional office environment. This role routinely uses standard office productivity machinery such as computers, keyboards and a mouse, laptops, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets and fax machines.
This is largely a sedentary role; however, some filing is required. This would require the ability to move files, open filing cabinets and bend or stand as necessary.
The ability to observe details at close range (within a few feet of the observer).
The person in this position frequently communicates with donors, colleagues, students, and general public. Must be able to communicate with others effectively.
Physical effort/lifting, such as up to 40 pounds.
Often travel requirements can include the following, evenings, weekends, and out of town overnights as a regular part of the job.

KU Endowment is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals to enable them to perform the essential functions of the job as regulated by ADA. If you require accommodation for any part of the application process or during employment, please contact humanresources@kuendowment.org to discuss your needs.

We’ve Got You Covered

KU Endowment offers a competitive salary with an excellent benefit package including:

100% employer-paid pension plan
Health, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) and Roth 401(k) matching program
Section 125 flexible benefits
Generous paid leave including holidays, personal and sick leave
Volunteer and community engagement opportunities
Paid Parental Leave
Life, AD&D, short- and long-term disability insurance
Legal & ID Theft protection
Critical Illness

KU education assistance
Free parking

Sounds good, right?
What’s next?

Please include your resume and cover letter when applying for this position on our website at https://www.kuendowment.org/careers.

new_jobs.description:
University of Colorado Anschutz

Department: Office of Advancement

Job Title:

Assistant or Associate Director of Development

Position #: 00826604 – Requisition #:
40694

Job Summary:

This is an open-rank position.
We are seeking to fill one Development Officer position, with the appointment made at either the Assistant Director or Associate Director level based on the selected candidate's experience, qualifications, and demonstrated skills.

Position Emphasis:

The University of Colorado Denver | Anschutz Medical Campus is a leading public research university serving more than 28,000 students across the Denver metro area and online. With 13 schools and colleges, 119 degree programs, and more than $400 million in annual research funding, CU Denver | Anschutz is recognized for academic excellence, healthcare innovation, and impactful research.

The Office of Advancement connects benefactor interests with university priorities to support education, research, and clinical care. Through fundraising, stewardship, and engagement, the office advances the mission of CU Anschutz and helps shape the future of healthcare.

We are a collaborative team of more than 60 fundraising, benefactor relations, and administrative professionals committed to advancing CU Anschutz and serving our benefactors.

Assistant Directors of Development build and maintain key relationships while providing fundraising and benefactor support to physician leaders, faculty, and staff. These positions recommend strategy and provide professional support to External Directors of Development and Advancement leadership.

Supervision Received: Reports to the Managing Director of Development
Supervision Exercised: No direct reports.

Key Responsibilities:

Training and Fundamental Skill Development (50%)

In close partnership with the Managing Director of Development:

Participates in fundraising training focused on benefactor engagement, discovery, stewardship, portfolio management, and development operations
Learns and practices the “art of fundraising,” including discovery conversations, thank-you calls, trust-building, and engagement strategies
Learns and practices the “science of fundraising,” including consistent outreach, timely follow-up, documentation standards, use of fundraising systems, prioritization of work, and related development operations
Builds working knowledge of CU Anschutz Medical Campus priorities, academic programs, fundraising processes, campus initiatives, talking points, faculty and hospital relations, fund agreements, gift processing, and related Advancement operations through guided learning, shadowing, and coaching
Develops comfort and confidence in fundraising language, outreach techniques, and benefactor conversations through supported practice

Thank-You Calls, Discovery Work, and Stewardship (Assistant – 30%)

Conducts timely thank‑you calls, personalized emails, and stewardship outreach to supporters to express appreciation, reinforce connection to CU Anschutz, and identify interest in further engagement
Completes discovery outreach, primarily through phone, to learn about benefactors’ interests and motivations
Initiates in-person visits with benefactors and collaborates with the Managing Director and senior development officers to strengthen relationships
Completes timely follow-up, schedules future engagement, and shares relevant information
Documents contact reports, discovery notes, and next steps accurately and promptly to support benefactor continuity and team strategy
Assists with proactive stewardship of leadership annual giving and mid-level benefactors with a focus on retention and engagement
Practices and implements proactive strategies and tools to move relationships and conversations forward

Associate Level (35%), all of the above and:

Independently leads benefactor conversations, including discovery, solicitation, and stewardship, with support from a senior gift officer when appropriate
Provides proactive cultivation and stewardship to retain and grow leadership-level and major gift benefactors year over year through independently developed plans and strategies
Creates individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies
Shares research updates, impact stories, and funding opportunities with benefactors
Serves as a trusted liaison to support productive benefactor engagement

Gift Conversations and Portfolio Work (Assistant – 15%)

Manages a portfolio of approximately 120-140 benefactors focused primarily on leadership annual gifts in the $500-$10,000 range, with goals co-created with and approved by leadership
Practices leadership-level and renewal gift solicitations with increasing independence
Participates in gift conversations led by senior development officers to gain exposure to benefactor strategy and proposal work
Identifies benefactors for continued cultivation and larger gift opportunities
Demonstrates professionalism in interactions with benefactors, colleagues, faculty, campus leadership, and other internal and external partners

Associate Level (35%), all of the above and:

Manages a major gift portfolio with accountability for strategy, progress, and results
Inspires benefactors to increased levels of giving, including renewal asks, asks under threshold, and pipeline-building asks, with a focus on gift conversations at $15,000+
Independently develops and executes solicitation plans, stewardship touchpoints, and long-term cultivation strategies toward larger gifts
Completes proposals, pledges, agreements, and follow-up activities accurately and timely
Uses fundraising systems and metrics to prioritize work and evaluate portfolio health
Documents benefactor strategies, contact reports, and next steps to support continuity, collaboration, and effective customer service with colleagues
Analyzes fundraising activity, portfolio performance, and benefactor engagement metrics to identify trends, assess progress toward goals, and inform future cultivation and solicitation strategies
Develops and implements long-term strategies for benefactor cultivation, stewardship, and pipeline growth, aligning individual and departmental fundraising efforts with institutional priorities
Evaluates fundraising effectiveness and benefactor engagement outcomes

Strategic Collaboration and Engagement with Internal and External Constituents (Associate – 25%)

Works closely with our Faculty Hospital Relations team to develop and maintain strong internal partnerships with faculty, campus leadership, and advancement colleagues to advance philanthropic priorities and benefactor relationships
Serves as a trusted liaison with benefactors ensuring values‑aligned engagement
Builds partnerships with Advancement teams including Communications, Stewardship, Events, and Alumni Relations
Partners closely with CU Anschutz external development officers to continue growth, learning and professional development
Contributes to a collaborative fundraising culture by sharing insights, supporting team strategy discussions, and aligning efforts across campus and central partners
Represents the University professionally in benefactor meetings, campus engagements, and select events, exercising sound judgment and discretion
Exercises sound judgment in managing donor conversations, including independently resolving issues when appropriate and engaging leadership or partners thoughtfully when needed
May informally mentor ADODs by modeling effective fundraising practices and contributing to a supportive learning environment

Other Duties (5%)

Represents the University at events to support the University and meet, cultivate, and steward benefactors
Performs various other duties or tasks as assigned and/or needed

Work Location:

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

Why Join Us:

Philanthropy accelerates discovery, supports students and faculty, and advances patient care. The CU Anschutz Office of Advancement partners with benefactors who want to make a lasting impact through education, research, and healthcare. Our team works collaboratively to connect supporters with meaningful opportunities to advance the university's mission.

At the Office of Advancement at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, we put our passions to work.

Why work for the University?

We have AMAZING benefits and offer exceptional amounts of holiday, vacation and sick leave! The University of Colorado offers an excellent benefits package including:

Medical: Multiple plan options
Dental: Multiple plan options

1-2 years managing portfolio or large list of prospect names

Strong written and verbal communication skills
Ability to build and maintain effective relationships across all organizational levels

Experience fostering an environment that values varied backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Yale New Haven Hospital is seeking an accomplished academic podiatric foot and ankle surgeon to serve as the Program Director of its CPME-accredited Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program. This is a unique opportunity to join one of the nation's premier academic health systems and help shape the education and development of future podiatric surgeons.

As Program Director, you'll provide strategic and educational leadership for a well-established residency program while maintaining an active clinical practice. The role is ideal for a physician who is passionate about resident education, mentorship, academic medicine, and advancing innovation in podiatric surgery. You'll collaborate closely with multidisciplinary faculty across Yale New Haven Health and the Yale School of Medicine, contributing to excellence in patient care, research, and physician training.

Yale New Haven Health is committed to fostering a culture guided by its core values of Integrity, Patient-Centered Care, Respect, Accountability, and Compassion, with a strong emphasis on academic excellence, collaboration, and delivering exceptional care to the communities it serves.

This position offers the opportunity to make a lasting impact on one of the country's respected podiatric residency programs while building an academic career within a nationally recognized healthcare system.

Responsibilities

Educational Leadership

Provide strategic leadership for all aspects of the residency program.
Develop, implement, and continuously enhance a comprehensive competency-based curriculum in podiatric medicine and foot and ankle surgery.
Foster resident development in clinical judgment, surgical technique, professionalism, communication, and lifelong learning.
Promote scholarly activity, quality improvement, and evidence-based practice.
Create a culture of educational excellence, innovation, patient safety, professionalism, and accountability.

Program Administration

Direct the overall administration of the residency program.
Maintain compliance with all Council on Podiatric Medical Education (CPME) accreditation standards, Yale New Haven Health policies, and Yale School of Medicine Graduate Medical Education requirements.
Oversee resident recruitment, orientation, evaluations, promotion, remediation, graduation, and disciplinary processes.
Supervise the Residency Program Coordinator and ensure efficient day-to-day operation of the residency program.
Lead annual program evaluation and continuous quality improvement initiatives.

Clinical Education

Coordinate resident clinical rotations throughout Yale New Haven Health and affiliated training institutions.
Ensure comprehensive operative and clinical experience across the full spectrum of podiatric medicine and foot and ankle surgery, including reconstructive surgery, trauma, diabetic limb preservation, sports medicine, wound care, and complex foot and ankle pathology.
Collaborate with faculty to maximize educational opportunities and progressive surgical responsibility.
Promote interdisciplinary education and collaborative patient care throughout the Yale New Haven Health System.

Faculty Development

Recruit, mentor, develop, and retain faculty committed to excellence in graduate medical education.
Foster faculty participation in teaching, mentorship, curriculum development, resident evaluation, scholarly activity, and educational innovation.
Support faculty development through mentorship and continuing educational opportunities.

Academic Appointment And Faculty Responsibilities

The Program Director is expected to serve as a respected physician-educator and academic leader dedicated to graduate medical education and the advancement of podiatric medicine and surgery.

Responsibilities Include

Provide outstanding clinical and surgical teaching in the operating room, ambulatory clinics, inpatient services, and formal didactic conferences.
Mentor residents in surgical technique, clinical decision-making, professionalism, ethics, leadership, and career development.
Promote scholarly activity through clinical research, quality improvement initiatives, publications, presentations, and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Participate in Graduate Medical Education initiatives, institutional committees, faculty development programs, and strategic educational planning.
Advance the academic mission and national reputation of the Yale New Haven Hospital Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program.

Qualifications

Education:

Doctor of Podiatric Medicine (DPM).

Licensure & Certification

Board Certification by the American Board of Foot and Ankle Surgery (ABFAS).
Eligible for unrestricted licensure to practice podiatric medicine in the State of Connecticut.
Eligible for appointment to the Yale New Haven Hospital Medical Staff with unrestricted clinical privileges.

Experience

Progressive leadership experience in graduate medical education.
Previous experience as a Program Director or Associate Program Director of a CPME-accredited Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program strongly preferred.
Demonstrated success in residency education, accreditation, faculty mentorship, and program development.
Academic appointment or eligibility for faculty appointment within the Yale School of Medicine preferred.

Leadership Competencies

Additional Information

The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate

Visionary and collaborative leadership.
A commitment to graduate medical education and the development of future leaders in podiatric medicine and surgery.
Excellence in clinical practice, surgical education, and patient-centered care.
Integrity, professionalism, accountability, and sound judgment.
Strategic thinking, innovation, and continuous quality improvement.
Commitment to mentorship, scholarship, diversity, inclusion, and lifelong learning.
The ability to advance the academic mission and national reputation of the Yale New Haven Hospital Podiatric Medicine and Surgery Residency Program.
